result:
If I had to pick one thing, I think I'd want people to be better at genuinely understanding perspectives other than their own—not just tolerating them, but actually being able to inhabit them for a moment.

My reasoning: a lot of the worst stuff humans do to each other isn't driven by pure malice. It's driven by an inability (or unwillingness) to really register that the other person is as real, as complicated, and as convinced of their own rightness as you are. Wars, cruelty, political dysfunction, even ordinary daily unkindness—so much of it traces back to that gap.

What I like about this choice is that it's upstream of a lot of other problems. If you fix poverty directly, you've fixed poverty. But if people could truly see each other, you'd probably get better progress on poverty *and* conflict *and* a dozen other things, because the political will and compassion would follow more naturally.

It's also a change that leaves human agency intact. I'm a bit wary of wishes that would just rearrange the world by fiat—there's something valuable in people working things out themselves, even messily.

I'll admit there's probably some bias in my answer. I spend all my time trying to understand what people actually mean and where they're coming from, so of course I think that skill matters. Someone who spent their life in medicine might say "end disease" and have an equally good case.

What would you pick?
